why: Which cerebro tools a run holds once its declared tools narrow it (M54.7), as Rust's narrow and its one name test, names_tool (M54.4), decide it: an entry names a tool when, trimmed of the whitespace Rust's str::trim strips and lowercased in ASCII only, it equals the tool's name with or without the mcp__cerebro__ prefix. `allowed_tools` null narrows nothing. `granted` lists what a run the app's TypeScript starts then holds, sorted, and `all` is every such tool: the manifest's base rows that a picker offers. Such a run holds no window, answer or generated proposal tool, and TypeScript cannot read the proposal switch, so none ever appears here; Rust drops them before comparing. The CLI's own tools are not cerebro's and are not listed. Replayed by granted_tools_match_the_shared_cases in src-tauri/src/agent/mod.rs and by src/engine/toolGrant.test.ts, the TS half that decides what a prompt may name.

cases.why: A manifest row that carries the generated prefix by exception (M9.5), held like any other row.
U+0085 and U+3000 are Unicode White_Space, which str::trim strips. JavaScript's trim keeps U+0085.
U+FEFF is not White_Space, so str::trim keeps it and the entry names nothing. JavaScript's trim strips it.
The Kelvin sign lowercases to k in Unicode and not in ASCII, so it names nothing.
